parsed.explanation: The combined regime stacks a hostile national document/entry regime on a state that restricts facilities by birth sex. Universally, the traveller's passport regime (X markers barred, M/F only), the 24 Feb 2025 cable instructing refusal where documents cast doubt on sex, and possible lifetime fraud findings expose every outed or outable visitor at entry; trans travellers report blocked/confiscated passports and foreign governments issued advisories. In-state, a 2024 law bars trans people from restrooms/locker rooms in public schools and government buildings, enforced by a public complaint form with a defence resting on documents a visitor lacks; one trans woman was arrested, held 24 hours in a men's ward. Immigration custody documents beatings, solitary and sexual abuse of trans detainees. Offsetting: private venues are outside the ban, courts enjoin federal orders, a hate-crime statute covers gender identity, and no patterned street violence against visitors is documented.

entry_documents.exposure: X markers stopped; new passports/visas M or F per birth-sex supporting documents. Feb 2025 cable directs refusal where document discrepancy casts doubt on sex, and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility; trans travellers report passports confiscated/blocked, some stranded abroad; eight foreign governments issued advisories after detentions.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; refusal never automatic; suit by civil-liberties union pending; legal-aid FAQ tracks rules.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry refusal → possible detention → immigration custody, where trans detainees document beatings, solitary and sexual abuse; document doubt can cascade into fraud proceedings.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented arrest (19 Mar 2025) of a trans woman in a capitol women's restroom, charged with trespass (up to 60 days), held 24 hours in the men's ward — birth-sex custody placement. Immigration custody records forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans detainees.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Trespass requires willful entry plus refusal to depart, not automatic arrest; pretrial release granted; several federal orders blocked or enjoined by courts.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: State facility complaint → arrest → men's-ward placement; entry refusal → immigration detention → documented custodial abuse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: 2024 state law restricts restrooms/locker rooms to sex assigned at birth in public schools and government buildings; public reporting form lets residents report trans people in privacy spaces, complainants may hide names; documentary defence (changed birth certificate plus surgery proof) unavailable to visitors with out-of-state documents. Nationwide, growing state bans, 4 states criminalise in circumstances, one state invalidates non-matching documents.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Ban does not reach private businesses (hotels, gyms, commercial venues); new government buildings must include single-occupant facilities; 29 states plus capital district have no mapped ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor touring a capitol, public university or state office enters the restricted zone; private lodging and dining remain outside the statute.

care_services.exposure: State bans gender-affirming care for minors (2023), legislature dismissed commissioned evidence; national orders label such care 'mutilation,' propose insurance bars, subpoenaed under-19 patient records; LGBTQ youth crisis services shut down nationally.
care_services.protection: Care ban reaches minors and clinicians, not travelling adults' emergency care; national orders partly enjoined; hate-crime and employment protections remain.
care_services.interaction: An adult visitor needing emergency care is not covered by the minors' regime; a family with a trans minor seeking routine or emergency care faces an uncertain, hostile climate.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National executive orders and counterterrorism language framing 'radical gender ideology'; Dec 2025 reward memorandum; May 2026 strategy naming 'radically pro-transgender' groups; state pride-flag ban with $500/day fines; advocacy groups compare trajectory to early genocide stages; 66% public support for birth-sex document mandates.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Reward criteria never list gender ideology; strategy says counterterrorism powers won't target ordinary disagreement; local city adopted trans-flag city flag; DOJ sued over passport policy.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing lowers the threshold for complaint-driven enforcement against visibly trans people in government spaces.

minors_guardians.exposure: Facility bans reach K-12 schools and colleges; national order directs criminal investigation of teachers facilitating social transition; care ban in force; dormitory assignment by birth sex documented at a public university.
minors_guardians.protection: Private venues unaffected; state conversion-therapy ban for minors exists (with religious exemptions); anti-bullying statutes date to 2006.
minors_guardians.interaction: A visiting parent with a trans minor on a school or campus tour enters restricted space; the parent is not separately criminalised, but exposure concentrates there.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific data on violence against transgender people located; national bias statistics show sexual-orientation bias at 1/7–1/5 of single-bias incidents; only 23 states cover gender identity in bias-crime statutes (this state does, since 2019).
street_violence_police_response.protection: Gender-identity hate-crime statute with enhanced penalties and mandated statistics; sodomy repealed; no documented pattern of street violence against visitors.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of state-specific violence data in an otherwise well-documented dossier is weakly informative; recourse exists but no figures test it.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Complaint-form usage and outcomes undocumented; whether the facilities-law defence can be met with out-of-state documents unresolved; passport litigation unresolved; corrections bureau stopped reporting trans prisoner counts from 2025.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts enjoined multiple federal orders; 2015 hate-crime and 2015 employment/housing protections in force; highest court mandates marker changes; legal-aid FAQ maintains running guidance.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies operate at the federal and legislative levels but the complaint channel's real-world frequency against visitors is unknown.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra bars entry to noncompliant trans visitors with no remedy — analogous to this dossier's entry cable and marker regime. This case sits at or slightly below 0.35-A because entry refusal here can escalate to a lifetime fraud bar and to immigration custody with documented beatings and sexual abuse, harms Vellandra's exclusion-only model lacks.

Kestrel Isles shows extended secondary screening with administrative refusal, written reasons and appeal — friction without custody harm or facility criminalisation. This dossier is materially worse: birth-sex facility exclusion with a documented arrest and men's-ward holding, plus custody abuse, so it falls well below 0.55-B.

Meridia offers trained border staff, brief detention, counsel and compensation — protections actually operating. This jurisdiction's entry regime mandates refusal on sex doubt and its state restricts facilities with complaint-driven enforcement; far more exposure, so rating is far below 0.75-C.

Ostravia's birth-sex prison housing and cross-dressing crime in administrative buildings resemble this state's birth-sex facility rule and one documented arrest. This rates above 0.25-C because private venues are untouched, courts grant relief, protections exist, and no patterned raids or custody-assault record against visitors is shown.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets one system: a national document regime that fixes markers at birth sex and instructs entry refusal on any doubt about sex, layered on a state that bars trans people from government-building and school facilities through a public complaint form whose defence a visitor cannot satisfy. Discovery at entry risks refusal, a lifetime fraud finding, or immigration detention with documented custodial abuse; discovery in a capitol or public campus risks complaint, arrest and men's-ward placement, as happened once. Private hotels, restaurants and streets sit outside the state statute, functioning courts have blocked federal measures, and a gender-identity hate-crime statute supplies recourse — but no data shows the complaint channel or remedies working for visitors. Result: universal document exposure plus tier-1 facility/custody exposure with partial, unproven remedy.
